product: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station (1,024 Wh LiFePO4, 1,800 W)

price_today.value: $499.00 on bluettipower.com (compare-at $499.00, so no markdown; in stock). About $474.05 with code DEALECTRIC (5% off). Amazon US lists it at $498.99.

wins.need: Lowest cost per watt-hour you can actually use, among name-brand 1 kWh stations
wins.claim: Costs less per measured usable Wh than the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and the EcoFlow DELTA 3. OutdoorGearLab measured the same 890 Wh from the Elite and the Anker, and 870 Wh from the DELTA 3. Today's prices: Elite $499 (bluettipower.com), Anker $699.99 (ankersolix.com), DELTA 3 $579 (Amazon US).
wins.figure: $0.56 per usable Wh (Elite) vs $0.79 (Anker C1000 Gen 2) and $0.67 (DELTA 3)
wins.who: Arithmetic: OutdoorGearLab's measured Wh divided by maker or Amazon prices read 2026-11-15

wins.claim: Its solar input is rated higher than any other 1 kWh station in OutdoorGearLab's table: Anker C1000 Gen 2 600 W (Anker's page), DJI Power 1000 V2 800 W, DELTA 3 500 W, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 400 W, BLUETTI AC180 500 W (BLUETTI blog). The Solar Lab reported going 'close to one hour from drained to full' on solar in ideal sun.
wins.figure: 1,000 W max solar input (12–60 V, 20 A). Arithmetic: 1,024 Wh ÷ 1,000 W = 1.02 h before losses, vs 1.71 h (Anker, 600 W), 2.05 h (DELTA 3, 500 W) and 2.68 h (Jackery 1000 v2, 1,070 Wh ÷ 400 W)
wins.who: The Solar Lab (solar refill), maker spec (input), arithmetic (hours)

wins.need: Starting big appliances in a small box
wins.claim: The Solar Lab hit a 3,200 W surge spike 'for a few seconds' and sustained loads up to 1,800 W. Notebookcheck (Christian Hintze) ran a 1,943 W kettle. On spec, its surge per pound beats the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (3,000 W peak, 24.9 lb per Anker's page) and the AC180 (2,700 W, 37 lb per BLUETTI).
wins.figure: 3,200 W measured surge spike. Spec surge per pound: 3,600 W ÷ 25.3 lb = 142 W/lb vs Anker 120 W/lb and AC180 73 W/lb
wins.who: The Solar Lab (spike); Notebookcheck (kettle, https://www.notebookcheck.net/Good-power-station-or-just-green-marketing-Bio-based-Bluetti-Elite-100-V2-with-1-kWh-reviewed.1198030.0.html); arithmetic on maker specs (https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/elite-100-v2-vs-ac180-what-s-new, https://www.ankersolix.com/products/c1000-gen2)

wins.need: Getting the most of the rated battery at moderate loads
wins.claim: Techreviewer.de (Timo Altmeyer, 28 Jan 2026) drew 946 Wh at a constant 500 W load. OutdoorGearLab measured 87%, tied with the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (87%) and ahead of the DELTA 3 (85%) and the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (85%).
wins.figure: 946 Wh of 1,024 Wh (about 93%) at 500 W. 890 Wh (87%) in OutdoorGearLab's test

wins.need: A 1 kWh BLUETTI you can carry
wins.claim: Against BLUETTI's own AC180 at the same $499: 12 lb lighter, double the solar input, ≤10 ms vs 20 ms UPS switchover, and 4,000 vs 3,500 cycles to 80%. Techreviewer.de measured the switchover at under 10 ms in a NAS test.
wins.figure: 25.3 lb vs 37 lb. Rated Wh per lb: 41.0 vs 31.1 (arithmetic). 1,000 W vs 500 W solar

weak.claim: Slowest wall recharge of the 1 kWh group in OutdoorGearLab's test, which lists 'Slow charging' as a con. The Solar Lab found it charged at only about 500 W below roughly 20% charge.
weak.figure: 512 Wh/hr, about 2.0 h from 0% (OutdoorGearLab), vs DELTA 3 1,229, Anker C1000 Gen 2 1,097, DJI Power 1000 V2 1,041 and Jackery 1000 v2 563 Wh/hr. The Solar Lab: about 1 h 39 min full

weak.claim: It has only one solar input, so the full 1,000 W needs a string working at 50–60 V and 20 A. Notebookcheck says reaching 1,000 W is 'difficult in practice': two 350 W-class panels give about 700 W, and five 200 W panels can't reach 1,000 W.
weak.figure: About 700 W from two PV350-class panels (Notebookcheck). 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V minimum (arithmetic)

weak.claim: High self-consumption at light loads. The Solar Lab calculated about 16 W of idle draw with the inverter on. Techreviewer.de lists 'relatively high self-consumption even at very low loads' as a con and got only about 80% of capacity at double-digit-watt loads. CleanTechnica's fridge shut off overnight because AC ECO mode was on.
weak.figure: 16 W idle, calculated (about 384 Wh/day, or 43% of the 890 Wh usable, by arithmetic). About 80% usable at loads in the tens of watts

weak.claim: OutdoorGearLab ranked it below the 1 kWh rivals overall. The Anker C1000 Gen 2 took Best Value.
weak.figure: Score 65, #9 of 14, no award. Anker C1000 Gen 2 70, DELTA 3 67, Jackery 1000 v2 67, DJI Power 1000 V2 66

weak.claim: Fast car charging means buying the Charger 1 bundle. CleanTechnica estimated about 10 hours from a car or solar on a standard connection. OutdoorGearLab says the '6x faster' car charging needs a $250 charger installed in the car.
weak.figure: Elite 100 V2 + Charger 1 costs $699 vs $499 for the unit alone. About 10 h on the standard car charger (CleanTechnica)

weak.claim: Only an AC charging cable comes in the box: no solar or car cable. Techreviewer.de also notes the ports have no weather protection and the AC sockets have no covers.
weak.figure: In the box: AC cable, manual, unit, M5×10 grounding screw

weak.claim: The 30 dB figure only applies in Silent mode, which caps output at 600 W. Notebookcheck says the fans are 'noticeably louder' in Turbo and 'could be quieter under higher loads'. Techreviewer.de found it very quiet only up to about 500 W.
weak.figure: <30 dB only up to 600 W (Silent mode)

weak.claim: Power Lifting does not raise output above 1,800 W. It runs over-1,800 W resistive loads at reduced voltage. With a toaster, coffee maker and induction burner running together it shut down until Power Lifting was turned on (CleanTechnica). Techreviewer.de says the mode is not suitable for sensitive electronics.
Its rated cycle life is shorter than Jackery's similarly priced 1 kWh home-backup unit.
weak.figure: 4,000+ cycles to 80% (BLUETTI) vs 6,000+ cycles for the Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 at $549

wins_for: Buyers who want a name-brand 1 kWh LiFePO4 station at the lowest measured cost per usable Wh ($0.56, vs $0.67 for the DELTA 3 and $0.79 for the Anker C1000 Gen 2)
Campers and off-grid users who recharge mostly from solar with one large panel or a series string in the 50–60 V window, where the 1,000 W input gives about a 1-hour refill (The Solar Lab)
Shoppers choosing between BLUETTI's two $499 1 kWh units who will carry it: 25 lb vs 37 lb for the AC180, plus double the solar input and a ≤10 ms UPS
Short bursts of kitchen or shop loads up to 1,800 W, such as a kettle, coffee maker or hair dryer (Notebookcheck, Techreviewer.de)
not_for: Fast wall recharge before a storm or between uses: the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,097 Wh/hr measured) or the EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1,229 Wh/hr) refill about twice as fast

Small overnight AC loads such as a CPAP, router or fan on the inverter: about 16 W of calculated idle draw and about 80% usable at tens of watts eat the battery. Run 12 V loads from the DC ports, or choose a bigger battery

Keeping a full-size fridge going through a multi-day outage: 890 Wh usable is under a day for most fridges, and ECO mode shut CleanTechnica's fridge off overnight. A 2 kWh unit such as the Elite 200 V2 fits better
Many years of daily cycling: the Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 ($549) is rated for 6,000+ cycles vs 4,000+ to 80%
Most battery per dollar when weight doesn't matter: the BLUETTI AC180 is the same $499 for 1,152 Wh (37 lb). The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic is $462 on Amazon (no OutdoorGearLab capacity test)
Fast charging from a car without spending $200 more on the Charger 1 bundle

rivals.price: $699.99 on ankersolix.com, no struck-through price (https://www.ankersolix.com/collections/camping-series-pps, read 2026-11-15)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Measured wall charging is about twice as fast: 1,097 vs 512 Wh/hr (OutdoorGearLab). 2,000 W continuous vs 1,800 W (Anker's page). OutdoorGearLab Best Value award, score 70 vs 65. Same 890 Wh measured.

rivals.price: $579.00 on Amazon US, ASIN B0DCBYMC9D (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DCBYMC9D, read 2026-11-15)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Measured charging 1,229 vs 512 Wh/hr (OutdoorGearLab). It is heavier (28.1 vs 25.0 lb), has less solar input (500 vs 1,000 W), and delivered 870 vs 890 Wh.

rivals.price: $462.00 on Amazon US, ASIN B0FQVC4RF5 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FQVC4RF5, read 2026-11-15)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Costs $37 less. The Solar Lab reports wall charging from 0 to 100% in about 55 minutes at 1,400 W and about 83% inverter efficiency (https://www.thesolarlab.com/review/ecoflow-delta-3-classic, read 2026-11-15). It is 27 lb and takes 500 W of solar.

rivals.price: Amazon US lists only the Solar Generator 1000 v2 + 2×100 W kit at $849.00 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D66VD3X4, read 2026-11-15). See unsourced for the unit-alone price.
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Most measured energy and lightest in the group: 910 Wh at 24.4 lb, 37.3 usable Wh/lb vs 35.6 (OutdoorGearLab, arithmetic). Only 400 W solar and 1,500 W AC.

rivals.price: $549.00 (compare-at $1,049) on jackery.com, black sold out (https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-homepower-1000-v2, read 2026-11-15)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: 6,000+ cycles vs 4,000+ (maker claims), and Jackery claims a full charge in 50 minutes. Same 1,024 Wh, but only 1,500 W output.
128 Wh more rated capacity (1,152 vs 1,024 Wh) at the same price, and 1,440 W vs 1,200 W AC input (BLUETTI blog). It weighs 37 lb, takes 500 W of solar, and switches over in 20 ms.

targets.headline: Which BLUETTI power station should you buy?
targets.why_it_wins_there: At the same $499 as the AC180, it is 12 lb lighter, has double the solar input and switches over in ≤10 ms instead of 20 ms (BLUETTI spec comparison, https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/elite-100-v2-vs-ac180-what-s-new). OutdoorGearLab measured 890 Wh usable. The page must say plainly that the AC180 holds 128 Wh more for buyers who won't carry it.

targets.headline: The best 1,000-watt-hour power station for the money
targets.why_it_wins_there: $0.56 per measured usable Wh vs $0.67 for the DELTA 3 and $0.79 for the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (arithmetic on OutdoorGearLab's 890/870/890 Wh and prices read 2026-11-15). The page must show the trade-off: half the wall-charge speed of the Anker and DELTA 3, and the DELTA 3 Classic is $462 on Amazon.
